b.e43effd6e3:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>P</c>ange, lingua, gloriósi
Prœlium certáminis,
Et super Crucis trophǽo
Dic triúmphum nóbilem,
Quáliter Redémptor orbis
Immolátus vícerit.

<h>D</h>e paréntis protoplásti
Fraude Factor cóndolens,
Quando pomi noxiális
Morsu in mortem córruit,
Ipse lignum tunc notávit,
Damna ligni ut sólveret.

<h>H</h>oc opus nostræ salútis
Ordo depopóscerat,
Multifórmis proditóris
Ars ut artem fálleret,
Et medélam ferret inde,
Hostis unde lǽserat.

<h>Q</h>uando venit ergo sacri
Plenitúdo témporis,
Missus est ab arce Patris
Natus, orbis Cónditor,
Atque ventre virgináli
Carne amíctus pródiit.

<h>V</h>agit infans inter arcta
Cónditus præsépia:
Membra pannis involúta
Virgo Mater álligat:
Et manus, pedésque, et crura
Stricta cingit fáscia.

<h>G</h>lória, et honor Deo
Usqueqáque Altíssimo,
Una Patri, Filióque;
Inclyto Paráclito:
Cui laus est et potéstas,
Per ætérna sǽcula.
Amen.
b.a8f191c38e:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>S</c>ing, my tongue, the glorious battle
Sing the last, the dread affray;
O'er the cross, the victor's trophy,
Sound the high triumphal lay:
Tell how Christ, the world's Redeemer,
As a victim won the day.

<h>G</h>od, his Maker, sorely grieving
That the first-made Adam fell,
When he ate the fruit of sorrow,
Whose reward was death and hell,
Noted then this wood, the ruin
Of the ancient wood to quell.

<h>F</h>or the work of our salvation
Needs would have his order so,
And the multiform deceiver's
Art by art would overthrow,
And from thence would bring the med'cine
Whence the insult of the foe.

<h>W</h>herefore, when the sacred fullness
Of the appointed time was come,
This world's Maker left his Father,
Sent the heav'nly mansion from,
And proceeded, God Incarnate,
Of the Virgin's holy womb.

<h>W</h>eeps the infant in the manger
That in Bethlehem's stable stands;
And his limbs the Virgin Mother
Doth compose in swaddling bands,
Meetly thus in linen folding
Of her God the feet and hands.

<h>T</h>o the Trinity be glory
Everlasting, as is meet;
Equal to the Father, equal
To the Son, and Paraclete:
Trinal Unity, whose praises
All created things repeat.
Amen.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<c>B</c>ut Mary, Lazarus' other sister, took a pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly, and anointed the Feet of Jesus, and wiped His Feet with her hair; and the house was filled with the odour of the ointment. We have now heard that which was done; let us search out the mystic meaning thereof. Whatsoever thou art that wilt be a faithful soul, seek with Mary to anoint the Feet of the Lord with costly ointment. This ointment was a figure of justice, and therefore is there said to have been a pound thereof, a pound being a weight used in scales..

Pistis Græce, fides Latíne dícitur. Quærébas operári justítiam. Justus ex fide vivit. Unge pedes Jesu bene vivéndo: Domínica sectáre vestígia. <r>Hymnus</r>
<c>L</c>ustris sex qui jam peráctis,
Tempus implens córporis,

Passióni déditus,
Agnus in Crucis levátur
Immolándus stípite.

<h>H</h>ic acétum, fel, arúndo,
Sputa, clavi, láncea:
Mite corpus perforátur,
Sanguis, unda prófluit:

<h>C</h>rux fidélis, inter omnes

<h>F</h>lecte ramos, arbor alta,

Quem dedit natívitas:
Ut supérni membra Regis
Miti tendas stípite.

Ferre sæcli prétium,
Atque portum præparáre
Nauta mundo náufrago,

Usquequáque altíssimo:
Una Patri, Filióque,

b.a42f643425:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>M</c>arch 23rd 2027, the 15th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>I</h>n Africa, the holy martyrs Victorian, Pro-consul of Carthage, and two brethren from Aquae Regiae, also two merchants, both named Frumentius, all in the persecution by the Vandals, were, [as writeth the African, Victor, Bishop of Utica] on account of the steadfastness of their Catholic confession, put to the most grievous torments under the Arian king Hunneric, and gloriously crowned, [in the year 484.]
<h>L</h>ikewise in Africa, the holy martyr Faithful.
<h>T</h>here also holy Felix and twenty others.
<h>A</h>t Caesarea, in Palestine, the holy martyrs Nicon, [a Neapolitan,] and ninety-nine others. [All suffered at Taormina, in Sicily, under Decius.]
<h>A</h>lso the holy martyrs Domitius, [a native of Phrygia,] Pelagia, Aquila, Eparchius, and Theodosia, [under Julian the Apostate.]
<h>A</h>t Lima, [in the year 1606,] in the kingdom of Peru, holy Turibius, Archbishop of that see, by whose work the faith and discipline of the church were spread abroad in America.
<h>A</h>t Antioch, the holy Priest Theodulus.
<h>A</h>t Caesarea, the holy Confessor Julian.
<h>I</h>n Campania, the holy monk Benedict, who was shut up by the Goths in a glowing furnace, but upon the morrow was found unhurt, [in the year 550.]
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Canticle: Magnificat</h>
<r>Ant.</r> I have power * to lay down my life: and to take it up again.
<r>Canticle of the Blessed Virgin</r>
<r>Luke 1:46-55</r>
§00.83742356bc
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> I have power to lay down my life: and to take it up again.
b.cc5a24567e:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>A</c>diuva nos, Deus, salutáris noster: et ad benefícia recolénda, quibus nos instauráre dignátus es, tríbue veníre gaudéntes.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.d1b2d0c950:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>H</c>elp us, O God of our salvation, and grant us grace to draw near with joy to the memorial of thy great mercies whereby Thou wast pleased to make us new creatures.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.0dbe0cbb8f:
<h>Canticum: Nunc dimittis</h>
<r>Ant.</r> O Rex glorióse inter Sanctos tuos, qui semper es laudábilis et tamen ineffábilis: tu in nobis es, Dómine, et nomen sanctum tuum invocátum est super nos: ne derelínquas nos Deus noster: ut in die judícii nos collocáre dignéris inter Sanctos et Eléctos tuos, Rex benedícte.
<r>Canticum Simeonis</r>
<r>Luc. 2:29-32</r>
§00.f0c002767a
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> O Rex glorióse inter Sanctos tuos, qui semper es laudábilis et tamen ineffábilis: tu in nobis es, Dómine, et nomen sanctum tuum invocátum est super nos: ne derelínquas nos Deus noster: ut in die judícii nos collocáre dignéris inter Sanctos et Eléctos tuos, Rex benedícte.
b.ba99451005:
<h>Canticle: Nunc dimittis</h>
<r>Ant.</r> O glorious King among thy Saints, who art ever to be praised and yet art ineffable: thou, O Lord, art among us, and thy holy name is called upon us: forsake us not, O our God; that in the day of judgement thou mayest vouchsafe to place us among thy Saints and thine Elect, O blessed King.
<r>Canticle of Simeon</r>
<r>Luke 2:29-32</r>
§00.89b4b60b5f
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> O glorious King among thy Saints, who art ever to be praised and yet art ineffable: thou, O Lord, art among us, and thy holy name is called upon us: forsake us not, O our God; that in the day of judgement thou mayest vouchsafe to place us among thy Saints and thine Elect, O blessed King.
b.a663c992a4:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>a, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui in tot advérsis ex nostra infirmitáte defícimus; intercedénte unigéniti Fílii tui passióne respirémus:
<h>Q</h>ui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.3e7593b9e9:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> Almighty God, Which knowest that we be set in such straits that we have no power of ourselves to help ourselves, we pray thee mercifully to relieve us, for whom continually pleadeth the suffering of thine Only Begotten Son.
<h>W</h>ho with thee liveth and reigneth, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
